story.title: FCC Approves SpaceX's Plan for 1 Million Satellites, Sparking Scientific Skepticism
story.summary: The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) has authorized SpaceX to deploy up to 1 million satellites intended to function as data centers in space. This decision, made during the Trump administration, has prompted skepticism and concern from some scientists regarding the feasibility and implications of such a large-scale satellite deployment.

event_overview.title: About Space Technology
event_overview.subject: Space Technology
event_overview.summary: SpaceX’s Starmind is a proposed non-geostationary-orbit constellation intended to operate as orbital data centers, processing data in space and using optical links to connect within the network and to Starlink. On November 25, 2026, the FCC’s Space Bureau granted SpaceX conditional, partial authorization for the system’s backup and emergency radio communications, subject to deployment, interference, coordination, and debris-related conditions.

facts.label: Applicant and proceeding
facts.value: Space Exploration Holdings, LLC (SpaceX) filed the application for its “SpaceX Orbital Data Center System,” later identified in the authorization as Starmind, on January 30, 2026; the FCC accepted it for filing and public comment on February 4, 2026.

facts.label: Regulator and legal scope
facts.value: The FCC Space Bureau’s November 25, 2026 order was granted in part and deferred in part. Its stated scope is authority for backup and emergency telemetry, tracking, and command radiofrequency communications—not a general certification that orbital data centers are technically or economically viable.

facts.label: System format
facts.value: The authorization covers up to 1,000,000 satellites in low Earth, non-geostationary orbit, in six orbital-shell groupings spanning altitudes from 500 to 1,002 kilometers. Starmind is intended to rely primarily on optical inter-satellite links, including links with Starlink satellites.

facts.label: Communications conditions
facts.value: Ka-band use at 18.8–19.3 GHz downlink and 28.6–29.1 GHz uplink is authorized only for backup and emergency command functions, on an unprotected, non-interference basis. SpaceX must cease operations causing documented harmful interference and coordinate with affected federal users.

facts.label: Build-out milestones
facts.value: The authorization becomes null and void unless SpaceX operates one satellite by November 25, 2033; 10% of the maximum constellation by November 25, 2035; 50% by November 25, 2038; and the remainder by November 25, 2040. The license term is 15 years beginning when SpaceX certifies its first Starmind satellite is operational under the authorization.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the FCC action and immediate scientific skepticism around it, not the full FCC docket, future launches or deployment, the project’s technical feasibility, or wider satellite-regulation developments.

related_stories.summary: A Maltese-flagged diesel tanker carrying approximately 7,000 tonnes of fuel capsized off the coast of Ibiza. While all 17 crew members were rescued, one later died in the hospital. Spanish authorities are now implementing a contingency plan to address potential marine pollution risks.

related_stories.title: Pittsburgh Steelers Release Aaron Rodgers Following Criticism of Coach
related_stories.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers have released quarterback Aaron Rodgers shortly after he publicly criticized head coach Mike McCarthy during an appearance on 'The Pat McAfee Show.' Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep in meetings and missing walkthroughs, leading to tensions within the team. Steelers president Art Rooney II stated that 'insubordination will not be tolerated' in light of the incident.

related_stories.title: Fuel Truck Fire in Cairo Kills 31 and Injures 21
related_stories.summary: A fuel tanker overturned on a major highway near Cairo, igniting a massive fire that engulfed over two dozen vehicles. At least 31 people have died and 21 others were injured in the incident. Authorities have detained a driver suspected of causing the crash, who reportedly confessed to speeding and clipping the tanker while overtaking traffic.

related_stories.title: Federal Judge Halts FCC's Early Review of ABC Broadcast Licenses
related_stories.summary: A federal judge has issued a temporary restraining order preventing the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) from conducting an early review of ABC's broadcast licenses. The judge's decision supports ABC's claim that the Trump administration's actions were intended to suppress the network's free speech rights. The ruling highlights concerns over the administration's public criticisms of the network.
